newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine shares close higher in see-saw trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine shares close higher in see-saw trade.

text.p: * Second-tiered property issues hog investor attention
Philippine shares ended another see-saw trading session on a slightly firmer note as buyers emerged only near the close of the session, brokers said.
"The market is still waiting for the real buying to come in. Foreigners have been buying selectively," Wilfred Son Keng Po, chief operating officer of Angping Securities, said.
The composite index rose by 8.60 points, or 0.28 percent, to close at 3,117.62.

Son Keng Po said the recent change in the composite index did not trigger a new wave of buying for the newly included index stocks, since most foreign brokerages had decided not to reposition their portfolio until next year.

Trading was concentrated mostly on secondary property issues such as Philippine Realty & Holdings which slid four centavos to 1.86 pesos and MRC Allied Industries which rose 15 centavos to 3.85 pesos.
Traders expected the index to drift within a narrow range until after the gross national product figures come out next week. - RAMONCITO DELA CRUZ 63 2 841-8937 Fax 8176267
